title: Ashaveri Evidence Capture (v1)
description: One piece of evidence's exact original bytes, held as they arrived, beside the context that made them verifiable at the instant they were taken in: the source they came from, our own acquisition time, the manifests the source served, the policy, verifier and format versions the check ran under, the signed collateral and validity context the bytes were appraised in, the trust references relied on, and the binding limits the verdict was reached under. A receipt points at its evidence with a digest, a timestamp and a URL, and a digest of a document nobody retained proves a hash existed rather than that the evidence survived; this document is what has to be handed over so that claim can be checked by somebody who does not trust the party that made it. Nothing writes one: this is the layout a collector has to be written against and the reading `parseCaptureRecord` and `assessCapture` in `packages/sdk/src/capture.ts` refuse. The shape is strict in both directions on purpose, as the policy document beside it is. Every block closes: a member the version names makes the document invalid rather than a document read with the unexpected member dropped, because a collector that wrote a field no reader knows was answering a question this record cannot ask. Absence is carried as a state, never as an omission: every context member says whether it is held, whether the source never produced it, or whether the collector failed to take it in, and those three are different outcomes that a reader must not merge. A held collateral slot owes ten members no other slot is asked for, because an answer is not a blob: it names the source it came under, the address it was asked at, the identity it claims, the instant it landed, that instant's own bound, the reading that weighed it, the span it reaches and the key it was kept under, and the header its issuer chain arrived in beside the digest of that header. Those are the parts a pack's custody entry is made of, member by member at `#/$defs/collateralObservation`, and a held slot in any other role may state them and owes none. There is deliberately no verdict field anywhere in this document, and none is defined for a future version to add: the keeping of bytes and their digest is what the writer asserts, and whether the signature over them holds is a check a reader repeats with its own pinned roots. A record that stated its own verification would let that assertion be read as the check.

v.description: Capture format version. A reader refuses a version it does not implement rather than reading the record as its own.

original.description: The bytes themselves, and what is claimed about them. Held as they arrived: no step between a source and this member may re-encode them, because a signature checked over a re-encoded document is checked over a document the source never produced.

sourceKind.description: Which of this estate's sources produced the bytes. A closed set: a new source arrives as a new capture version, because a reader that fell through an unknown kind to its default handling would assess a document it holds no rules for.

sourceId.description: The source's own name for itself as it served the bytes, an instance id or an endpoint. What the bytes are claimed to come from, not proof they did.

bytes.description: Unpadded base64url of the exact bytes as they arrived, in the one spelling that decodes back to them: the tail bits of a short last group are free, and a record written by a second encoder can carry the same bytes in a spelling no reader reproduces.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of exactly those bytes, and nothing else. A reader recomputes it and refuses the record when the two disagree, which is what makes a structurally equivalent re-serialization a refusal rather than an equal.

byteCount.description: How many bytes `bytes` decodes to. Stated so that a reader can name the disagreement when a record says one length and carries another.

signedBySource.description: Our assertion that the source signed these bytes. Stated either way rather than left out, because an omitted claim and a denied one are different records. Nothing here says the signature holds.

signatureEmbedded.description: True when the signature travels inside `bytes`, as a COSE_Sign1 carries its own, and false when the source served it apart. Read together with signedBySource this decides whether a signature slot has to be held, so a record cannot claim a signature and carry none.

signature.description: The detached signature, and the presence state of it. Only a record that claims a signature it does not carry inside its bytes has one, and only one whose slot says held is a record that carries it.

acquired.description: When the bytes came into our hands, on our clock, kept apart from when the source says they were made. Both are stated because the two disagreeing is information, and one number could not hold it.

at.description: Unix seconds on the collector's clock at the instant the bytes were taken in. This is the stamp our own claim of custody is dated by, and it is not the source's.

sourceStatedAt.description: Unix seconds, the timestamp the source claimed for these bytes, or null when the source claimed none. A claim, and the one a reader is not asked to believe: it is here so that a document dated after it was collected is visible rather than smoothed over.

manifests.description: The original manifests the source served at that instant, as they arrived. One role because this estate serves one deployment manifest; a second role is a new version rather than an extra member, since a reader that ignored one would be silent about what it did not look at.

deployment.description: The document at `/deployment-manifest` as served. The manifest is what pins are read from, so a capture without it says so in one of the two honest ways.

check.description: The rules the check ran under, as versions and as a digest. This block is what lets a verdict drawn in 2027 be read against the rules it was reached under rather than against whatever is current on the day somebody opens the record.

policyVersion.description: Which verification policy document version the check read. The reader implements one and refuses a record that names another.

policyDigest.description: SHA-256 of the policy document the check actually loaded, in its canonical re-encoding, or null when the check ran with no policy file at all. A reader may conclude which pins were in force and no more.

receiptFormatVersion.description: Which receipt format version the check read. The version decides which members exist, so a verdict about one version is not a verdict about another and a record has to say which it answered for. The format declares one payload version, `1`, and it carries the marking, the stamp disclosure, the collateral anchor and the item list: a record naming 1 is the ordinary output of a check run against an emitting deployment. A version outside this list is refused by the reader rather than read as the nearest one inside it, and the integers the payload retired name documents no reader of this build can open.

verifierVersion.description: Which verifier build ran the check. An attribution of a procedure, not a claim that the procedure was right: a reader re-runs it rather than trusting this string.

appraisedAt.description: Unix seconds on the collector's clock when the appraisal of this context ran. A reader refuses to place a record whose appraisal precedes its acquisition, and reports it unassessed.

context.description: What the bytes were appraised against. Both members are required and both carry a presence state, because a reader's verdict is only as good as what it can see was left out, and silence is not a state.

collateral.description: The signed collateral: the vendor certificate chain the platform report was chained to, as the source served it. A record holding none, or saying the source never produced one, reads as qualified or unassessed, and never as a pass. A held one is the answer to a question somebody asked somewhere: the eight members `#/$defs/collateralSlot` names state where, when, under whose name and over what span, and they are what a stranger can weigh or re-ask.

validity.description: The validity context the collateral was appraised in: the window and the appraisal a verifier recorded at that instant. Validity is a function of the day an appraisal ran, so a verdict without it is a verdict about nothing in particular.

trust.description: Who the check was willing to believe, and how far it was willing to lean on a clock. Both are read against the caller's own pins by the reader rather than accepted, which is the whole point of a stranger being able to run this record.

roots.description: The trust references the verdict relied on, one entry per vendor family consulted. An empty list says the check consulted none, which for any document claiming a signature is a record of an unverified signature.

family.description: Which vendor family, named exactly as a pinning policy names it.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the root bytes the check used, or null when it used a root bundled by its own library and did not name it. A reader compares it against the caller's pinned roots and never against a default of its own.

limits.description: The binding limits the verdict was reached under, spelled the two ways a policy document spells a window: a whole number of seconds, or null where the check named none of its own. A null is not a window that stayed open. The reader runs its own windows and reports a difference rather than inheriting this one.

maxReceiptAgeSeconds.description: How far a receipt's issuance stamp was allowed to sit from the checking clock.

maxEvidenceAgeSeconds.description: How far the evidence timestamp was allowed to sit from the checking clock.

digest.description: A SHA-256 digest, lowercase hex, 64 characters.

origin.description: Which source declaration an answer came under, named the way that declaration names itself. Required of a held collateral slot: bytes that name no source are a blob, and a reader has nothing to go and re-ask.

request.description: The address the answer was asked at, the request as it was framed rather than as an answer redirects to it, which is the member a reference names so a stranger can go and ask again. Bounded at 2,048 bytes of UTF-8, the ceiling the reference layout carries for an address, because a stated address past that ceiling is a record whose bytes can be kept and never pointed at: the bound is the reference's own and not a number this layout invented. It is a count of bytes and no JSON Schema keyword counts bytes, so the reader holds the rule and `docs/capture-v1.md` names which authority binds which rule.

identity.description: The identity the signed answer names for itself, or null where the answer names none. Both are statements, and an empty object is neither.

observedAt.description: Unix seconds, whole, the instant the last byte of this answer landed on the clock of the process that took it in. Not `acquired.at`, which is this collector's own clock and a different event, and not a fraction: an instant stated in no unit is a bound nobody can weigh against a window.

sourceUncertaintySeconds.description: How far the clock behind `observedAt` may stand from the instant it names, in whole seconds, or null where nobody measured it. A bound and not an instant. A null is a statement that no number was ever established, which is not the same reading as zero and is not a window that stayed open.

chainSha256.description: SHA-256 of the response header that carried an answer's issuer chain, as that header arrived. A reader recomputes it over `chainBytes` and refuses the two when they disagree, which is the same rule the bytes of an original are read by.

chainBytes.description: That header itself, unpadded base64url, as it arrived. The two halves of a chain come together or not at all: bytes no one can name a digest of are bytes no later reader can be shown, and a digest of a header nobody kept is a statement about nothing but a hash. An empty spelling is refused as one header would be, because a header of no bytes carried no chain.

weighedBy.description: Which reading weighed an answer: `served` where the signature and the issuer chain arrive apart from the body, `embedded` where the signature travels inside the bytes it signs. The source's own declaration settles this and a body does not, because a wrapper that starts with a brace and a token that starts with base64url are the same text to anything that looks.

window.description: How far an answer's own signed statement reaches: from included, to excluded. A statement about time, read off the bytes the slot holds, and not a claim that the span is still open.

cacheKey.description: The key an answer was kept under, spelled from the members that decide which question a kept blob answers, so a reader can tell which entry of a store a record is describing. An appraisal instant is deliberately absent from it: the same bytes are the same answer whichever moment they are read against.

collateralObservation.description: The eight facts a held collateral slot states about the answer its bytes are: where it came from, where it was asked, what it names itself, when it landed, how far that instant may stand, which reading weighed it, how far it reaches and which key it was kept under. A held slot outside the collateral role owes none of them. These are the parts of a custody reference, and the entry a pack makes from a held collateral slot takes them in order: `origin` becomes its `o`, `request` its `u`, `identity` its `i`, `observedAt` its `s`, `sourceUncertaintySeconds` its `n`, `weighedBy` its `a`, `window` its `w` and `cacheKey` its `y`, while the slot's own `sha256` is the entry's `b` and the chain's two halves together are its `c`. Which anchor slot of which receipt an entry answers is the entry's own statement and is named by no member of this record.

chainPair.description: The issuer chain's header and its digest, which arrive together or not at all. Stated as a rule of its own because it binds two members and no keyword that closes a block can say that.

held.description: A context member this record holds, as the bytes that arrived and the digest of exactly those bytes. Beside those four, a held slot may state what its bytes are an answer to: the ten members this definition names, which belong to a collateral slot and to no other, because a deployment manifest and a detached signature are not answers a source gave. Which slot owes them is a rule about a role, and this definition serves four roles, so the eight are required at `#/$defs/collateralObservation`, applied by `#/$defs/collateralSlot`, and an absent slot that borrows one of them is refused by `#/$defs/absent` closing at two members. Two rules in this family are ones no JSON Schema states, so the reader holds them: the digest a chain states has to be the digest of the chain bytes beside it, and unpadded base64url has one spelling a reader reproduces rather than any that decodes. A third is a count of bytes, which no keyword of this document version makes: the address a held slot states is bounded at what a reference can carry.

bytes.description: Unpadded base64url of the bytes as they arrived, in the one spelling that decodes back to them.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of those bytes. Recomputed by a reader, never read off this member.

collateralIdentity.description: The identity a signed answer names for itself, copied out of the answer rather than sorted into a label this record would prefer.

cpuType.description: The CPU type the answer claims to cover, in the answer's own words, or null where the document indexes nothing by one.

vendorStatus.description: The vendor's own status text beside what was asked. A word the source wrote, and the only reading of it this record states is the one the bytes carry.

signedWindow.description: The span a signed statement reaches, in whole unix seconds, from included and to excluded, which is how this estate's windows are read everywhere else.

from.description: The instant the statement begins to reach.

absent.description: A context member this record does not hold, and which of the two reasons applies. A reason is required: an absence nobody explained is indistinguishable from a hole, and the record exists to keep those apart.

presence.description: `absent-at-source` is a statement about the world: this source never produced it. `not-taken-in` is a statement about the collector: it may have existed and nobody put it in the record. They read differently and a reader reports them apart, the first as a qualified verdict and the second as unassessed.

reason.description: One line in the collector's own words about what it saw.

slot.description: One piece of context and its presence state. The three states are exhaustive and closed, so every absence in a capture record is one somebody wrote down.

collateralSlot.description: The slot that holds the signed collateral the bytes were appraised against. A held one owes the eight facts a reader needs in order to go and re-ask the answer it holds; an absent one owes the reason and nothing else. This is the one place in the layout where a role decides a requirement, and the reader refuses a held collateral slot missing any of them, member by member, naming the one that is absent. A held one is also the whole of what a pack's custody entry is made from, member by member in the sentence at `#/$defs/collateralObservation`.
